hypotheses.justification: The statement doesn't need Finite ι'. Here `b'.toMatrix b : Matrix ι' ι R` is defined by `fun i j ↦ b'.repr (b j) i`, as the definition at line 51 of Basis.lean shows. The product `*ᵥ` sums only over the column index ι, which is covered by the variable `[Fintype ι]`. No finiteness of the row index ι' is used. For each i : ι', the i-th entry of the left side is `∑ j, b'.repr (b j) i * b.repr m j`. This equals `b'.repr (∑ j, b.repr m j • b j) i`, which is `b'.repr m i` by `b.sum_repr`. The argument works for any ι', including empty or infinite ι'. The proof can be done directly with `ext i; simp [Matrix.mulVec, dotProduct, Basis.toMatrix_apply, ...]`, rewriting with `map_sum`, `map_smul` and `Basis.sum_repr`. This is the same kind of computation as line 105 of the file, which is `simp_rw [e.toMatrix_apply, e.sum_repr]`. The current proof's detour through `LinearMap.toMatrix` is the only reason it needs Finite ι' (and the `Fintype ι'` it extracts from it).
